notes: From T1 to T8 the Runner made 4-5 HQ runs per turn at 1 credit, seeing the same Game Over/Oppo Research/Daily Quest, and took a tag from Increased Drop Rates on every one without ever drawing or building economy. It ignored the advanced card in Server 1 on T2 (Post-Truth Dividend, scored T3), then spent T9-T15 clicking credits to clear tags and facechecked N-Pot on T15 while the Corp walked to 7 points.

Against a Runner that only clicked for credits, the Corp sank about 12 advances into the Server 1 card (T10-T23) without scoring it. It left Sericulture Expansion naked in Server 5 (stolen T15), put agendas behind a lone Vicsek (T17) and a lone Ivik (T18), and on T23 advanced the naked Hybrid Release in Server 10 only once instead of scoring it, so it was stolen for the loss.

The Runner clicked for credits nearly every turn from T2 to T16, reaching 68 credits with a full grip and no breaker installed until Buzzsaw on T17. Meanwhile it facechecked ETR ice with no breakers (Akhet T3, Descent T9 and T14, Envelopment T13) and never pressured R&D or HQ until T17-18, after the Corp was nearly done scoring.

This was a solid game: Vertigo blocked steals on R&D, and the Corp scored Méliès (Seamless Launch, T6), Project Ingatan (T7), Superconducting Hub (T11) and Architect Deployment Test (T12) from the Hagen remotes. Minor issues were the naked Nico Campaign trashed on T2, three clicks for credits on T3, and running at 0 credits for several turns (T7-T12).

The Runner applied focused R&D pressure with Concerto, Bravado, Window of Opportunity and Jailbreak, stealing four agendas for a T6 win, and correctly cleared an Oppo Research tag on T3. The only quibble is the early HQ facecheck into N-Pot on T1.

From T7 to T13, and again on T16, the Corp did nothing but click for credits, discarding a card every turn and banking 31 credits before it installed anything. Early on it spent its money on campaigns while R&D ice sat unrezzed, so Superconducting Hub (T2) and Architect Deployment Test (T3) were stolen; later Megaprix went behind a lone Eli 1.0 that the Runner already broke (stolen T22), though the Corp still won on T24.

The Runner set up well (Rigging Up into Unity, Dr. Nuka, Gauss) and hammered R&D and HQ for a T6 win. On T4 Dr. Nuka drew 3 into a full grip, which forced 3 discards, and it accepted a lot of Funhouse tags; that was only safe because the Corp was broke.

The Runner repeated runs that saw only the same cards (HQ on T1-T2, R&D x4 on T5 and T7). After stealing 3 points on T8, it clicked for credits every turn from T9 to T22, reaching 66 credits without installing a single breaker. The Corp sat on 6 points, the Runner checked Server 3 only once (Tree Line, T21), and the T23 Transport Monopoly score went unchallenged.

For the whole game R&D was guarded by a lone Konjin, which does nothing without other ice, and the Corp always bid 0 on the psi game, so the Runner took See How They Run (T8, T18) and Lotus Haze (T21) from R&D. The Corp sat at 0-3 credits for most of the game, Sisyphus Protocol sat at 2 advancements behind Saisentan until it was stolen T10, and the Corp played Neurospike for no effect on T13.

The Runner's Finality multi-access plus sabotage on T1 crippled the Corp, but the Corp then left R&D with only a lone Konjin (always bidding 0) through T4. It spent T2 clicking for credits and T3 installing in a new remote rather than adding R&D ice, and lost to R&D runs on T4.

The Corp built a sensible economy with Spin Doctor and Hedge Fund and scored Embedded Reporting on T5. However, it put the 3-point Next Big Thing behind a single cheap Ping on T4 (stolen T5 by Gauss) and left Tomorrow's Headline at 1 advancement behind Mestnichestvo on T6 (stolen). A second Tomorrow's Headline was then taken from HQ on T7.

On T1 the Runner facechecked HQ into Ballista, which trashed Buzzsaw, then facechecked Akhet on T2 and Afshar on T4. On T8 it ran into the known Ballista with only 2 credits and lost Boi-tatá, then spent T9-T14 rebuilding while the Corp scored to 6, and its late steals came too late.

On T1 the Corp spent all 5 credits rezzing Mestnichestvo and then played the whole game on 0-5 credits with no economy cards, clicking for credits and discarding on T7 and T9. R&D had only a single Ping all game (Tomorrow's Headline stolen T3, Next Big Thing T9), and Embedded Reporting was stolen from HQ on T8 after Tāo swaps.

The Runner made repeated HQ runs that saw the same Urtica Cipher/Vampyronassa (T1, T3) and facechecked Server 2 on T5, taking 4 net damage from Vampyronassa and Urtica. It then ran into the known, unbreakable Vampyronassa twice on T10 and again on T11 and T12, jacking out each time after 2 net damage. On T15 it ran into the already-seen Saisentan with a tiny grip and no counters left on Revolver and was flatlined.

The Runner made reasonable checks of naked remotes, though running the 1-advanced Server 2 on T3 hit Urtica Cipher for 3 cards (including Red Team) and Mavirus caught it twice. From there it steadily pressured HQ through Konjin with Carpe Diem and Info Bounty for a T10 win.

On T3 the Corp used Architect Deployment Test to put Megaprix Qualifier in a naked remote while broke (stolen immediately), then left Architect Deployment Test behind a lone Wave in Server 3 (stolen T6). It played most of the game on 0-2 credits. On T13 an Ansel 1.0 install apparently trashed the advanced Méliès in Server 3 into an unprotected Archives, where the Runner took it on T13-T14 for the win.

The Runner exploited a weakly defended HQ well, using Banner to get through Envelopment on T4 and Akhet on T7 and trading Buzzsaw to steal SDS Drone Deployment on T4. The only blemish was a low-credit facecheck into Afshar on Server 1 on T6.

The Corp dumped agendas into an unprotected Archives through the T4 draw-then-discard, Hafrún's HQ trash and AU Co. mills, and the Runner took Project Yagi-Uda and Hybrid Release from there on T8. It then sat at 0-2 credits while Sericulture Expansion idled behind Ivik (stolen T9), and on T10 it repeated the same remote with Fujii Asset Retrieval, which was stolen for the loss.

Early on the Corp clicked for credits for whole turns (T7, T8) while holding several agendas, and lost Megaprix (T10) and Architect Deployment Test (T11) from HQ. It installed Project Ingatan behind a lone Vertigo (T12) and Superconducting Hub behind a lone Drafter (T13), neither of which ends the run, and both were stolen. Later it stabilized with Ansel 1.0 and fast-advance scores (T14, T17, T22, T24) to win.

The Runner never installed a program and clicked for credits nearly every turn from T3 to T20 with a full grip, reaching 53 credits. On T12 it would not pay 3 to get through Grubber with 26 credits, and that agenda (Oracle Thinktank) was scored T15; it also took Funhouse and F2P tags rather than pay. It won only because the Corp left agendas naked or behind bypassable ice (T6, T10, T21).
